title: Herbivory enhances cadmium foraging in the invasive hyperaccumulating plant Phytolacca americana
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Biological invasions and heavy metal pollution are two pervasive environmental challenges threatening global ecosystems. While the elemental defence hypothesis posits that certain plants accumulate heavy metals to deter herbivores, it remains unclear whether invasive hyperaccumulators actively forage for these toxic elements and whether such below-ground behaviour is dynamically induced by above-ground biotic stress. Here, we investigated the foraging behaviour of the invasive hyperaccumulator Phytolacca americana in a rhizobox experiment simulating a dual-stress environment of heterogeneous cadmium (Cd) distribution and Spodoptera litura herbivory. We considered root morphological responses and employed integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We found that P. americana preferentially allocated root biomass to Cd-enriched soil patches when exposed to cadmium. Notably, above-ground insect herbivory significantly amplified this below-ground Cd foraging response. The interaction between Cd stress and herbivory markedly altered root morphology. Cd accumulated primarily in fine roots, where plants optimized their specific root length and tissue density to efficiently exploit Cd-rich zones. Integrated molecular analyses revealed that Cd treatment significantly suppressed cytokinin levels in the roots. This hormonal shift likely promotes lateral root formation and accelerates heavy metal sequestration. Our results demonstrate that above-ground biotic interactions can actively drive below-ground heavy metal foraging strategies in invasive plants, manifesting as a complex morphological plasticity mediated by cytokinin signalling. More broadly, our study highlights how synergistic responses to multiple environmental stressors can enhance the adaptive capacity and ecological success of invasive species in contaminated habitats.

摘要

生物入侵与重金属污染是威胁全球生态系统的两类普遍环境问题。元素防御假说认为，某些植物可通过积累重金属抵御植食性动物，但入侵性超富集植物是否会主动觅取这些有毒元素，以及这种地下行为是否受到地上生物胁迫的诱导，目前尚不清楚。 本研究通过根箱实验模拟镉(Cd)异质分布与斜纹夜蛾(Spodoptera litura)取食的双重胁迫环境，探究了入侵性超富集植物美洲商陆(Phytolacca americana)的觅食行为，解析其根系形态响应，并结合转录组学与代谢组学分析揭示其内在机制。 结果表明，在镉处理条件下，美洲商陆优先将根系生物量分配至镉富集土壤斑块，而地上昆虫取食会进一步增强这一地下镉觅食响应；镉胁迫与植食作用的交互显著改变了根系形态。镉主要积累于细根，植株通过优化比根长与组织密度高效利用富镉区域。转录-代谢联合分析结果显示，镉处理显著降低了根系细胞分裂素水平，这一激素变化可能促进侧根形成并提高重金属觅食效应。 上述结果表明，地上生物互作可主动驱动入侵植物的地下重金属觅食策略，该策略表现为由细胞分裂素信号介导的复杂形态可塑性。本研究揭示了对多重环境胁迫的协同响应如何提升入侵物种在污染生境中的适应性与生态优势。
